correctness.rationale: Geometric dot-product tests for all four foot normals and both nonautomatic vertex normals reduce the count to four affine inequalities. A separate critical-point alternation argument forces \(N=2\) times the number of side-foot normals, so exactly 4,6,8 occur. The affine (s,t) map of determinant 1-c² maps the eight-normal chamber bijectively onto a rectangle inside the unit square; elementary independent-uniform probabilities give the mean and determine the remaining masses. Piecewise derivative signs give uniqueness and sharpness of aspect extrema. 87 exact rational chamber decompositions and 1250 direct Euclidean pointwise checks pass (check_normals.py).

value.rationale: A full natural two-parameter family has a complete geometric-probability distribution with a sharp support collapse at \(cq=1\). The six-normal probability has a unique peak, the four-normal mass a unique valley, and the mean has a sharp rhombus extremum and thin-body limit. This quantifies Euclidean shape dependence well beyond the known universal mean upper bound or a mere pointwise enumeration.
